chain_class: C1 — JS-bridge RCE (addJavascriptInterface, CVE-2012-6636 family; historical, already-patched, reproduced on a deliberately vulnerable build per policy §7)
chain: QR URL sheet -> scan/open (physical slot or load_url.sh) -> emulator WebView (targetSdk-16 rig app) -> page JS -> vulnerable JS bridge -> app-process command execution -> TCP session callback to Kali-side listener stub
policy: docs/governance/policy.md §1 lab-only, §2 benign demo bodies / no default endpoints, §7 historical-patched-only. Emulator + owned devices ONLY.

target.note_on_api_level: API 22 boots a targetSdk-16 APK (no install-time targetSdk block) and keeps the C1 reflection window open for legacy-target apps; the platform-side fix landed in API 17 keyed on app targetSdk.
target.app_build: physical slot: open mobile/rig/target-app in Android Studio -> Build > Build APK(s)

steps.action: physical slot: install Android Studio + SDK cmdline-tools + platform-tools
physical slot: build + install the rig target app
start the Kali-side session listener (explicit host/port only)
serve the staging dir on the Kali box
copy payload.example.html to payload.html with YOUR lab host, then print its URL as a QR sheet
U stage: open the URL on the emulator (adb simulates what a QR-scanner app hands the OS; a physical scan of the printed sheet is the optional human step)
verify session on the Kali side
steps.cmd: listener prints: session N proof: 'P6RIG-SESSION device=<Build.FINGERPRINT>' then 'VERIFIED'

expected_logcat_markers: P6RIG BRIDGE_EXEC cmd=log -p i -t P6RIGQR stage_e_exec_ok
control_arm_expected: opening the same URL in the stock emulator browser (no --pkg) must NOT emit any BRIDGE_* marker — this negative control proves the marker set belongs to the vulnerable bridge class, not to generic page activity.
telemetry_to_capture: adb logcat -s P6RIG P6RIGQR (marker timeline, timestamps in order U->E->C)
listener_stub.py session log (Kali-side proof line + peer IP/port + wall-clock)
adb shell dumpsys package com.qrcompromise.p6rig (targetSdk=16 evidence for the C1 gate)
run wall-clock start/end so Stage-2 timing analysis can be layered on top
